newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Deka/ECT restart Bell's Rotterdam terminal.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Deka/ECT restart Bell's Rotterdam terminal.

text.p: Dutch Deka and European Combined Terminals (ECT) will restart the Bell Mertens container terminal on Tuesday under the new name Rotterdam Shortsea Terminal (RST), ECT and Deka said on Monday.
The terminal was a unit of bankrupt Irish group Bell Lines.
The restart comes after the workforce agreed the social plan which had been a sticking point in negotiations last week. RST will begin with 99 employees, 28 of them temporary.
Last Friday, Deka/ECT reached agreement with Bell liquidators to take possession of the Mertens terminal's five cranes.
Deka is to take a two-thirds participation and ECT a third.
Deka is a unit of unlisted Rotterdam firms Steinweg and Lehnkering Montan.
ECT is owned by Dutch transport groups Nedlloyd, Pakhoed, Internatio-Mueller and by state-owned Dutch Railways.
The Bell Mertens terminal started operations about a year ago and handles around 260,000 containers a year, mostly for short sea routes from Britain and Ireland to Rotterdam.
Waterford-based Bell Lines went into liquidation on July 4 with debts of around 40 million Irish pounds.
